data.name: Milo
data.gender_notes: Milo is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek 'milos', meaning 'mild' or 'merciful'. In Roman mythology, Milo was a soldier who saved the life of the Roman consul. In Christianity, Milo is a saint who is believed to have saved the lives of many pilgrims. The name Milo carries the meaning “Soldier, lover, or merciful” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Milo usually hope their child will grow to embody soldier, lover, or merciful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Milo belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Soldier, lover, or merciful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Milo total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: מילו
in_hebrew.meaning: מילה הלטינית שמשמעותה חייל, איש צבא
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מילו הוא שם שמקורו בלטינית, ומשמעותו חייל, איש צבא. השם מופיע בתקופה הרומית והיה נפוץ בקרב חיילים וגברים חזקים. עם הזמן, השם אומץ על ידי הנוצרים והפך לשם פופולרי בקרב המאמינים.

in_greek.name: Μίλω
in_greek.meaning: όνομα που σημαίνει στρατιώτης, άνθρωπος πολεμικός
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μίλω προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη 'miles', που σημαίνει στρατιώτης. Στην αρχαία Ελλάδα, το όνομα αυτό δεν ήταν πολύ κοινό, αλλά με την έλευση του Χριστιανισμού, το όνομα άρχισε να χρησιμοποιείται ευρέως ανάμεσα στους πιστούς.

in_latin.name: Milo
in_latin.meaning: meaning soldier, warrior, strong and powerful
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Milo originates from the Latin word 'miles', meaning soldier or warrior. In ancient Rome, the name was popular among soldiers and strong men. As Christianity spread, the name Milo became a popular choice among believers, symbolizing strength and courage in faith.

in_english.name: Milo
in_english.meaning: Soldier, warrior, or strong and powerful individual
in_english.long_meaning: The name Milo has its roots in Latin, derived from 'miles', meaning soldier or warrior. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, the name Milo has been associated with strength and courage, values highly regarded in Christian tradition. Historically, the name was popularized in ancient Rome and later adopted by Christians, symbolizing a strong and devoted follower of faith. Today, Milo remains a popular name across various Christian cultures, reflecting a balance of strength and spirituality.

data.cultural_impact: Milo is a name that has roots in both Greek and Roman mythology. In Greek mythology, Milo is a name associated with mildness or mercy. In Roman mythology, Milo is known as a soldier who saved the life of the Roman consul, demonstrating bravery and selflessness. These cultural associations point to a name with connotations of strength, kindness, and courage.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Milo also holds spiritual significance in Christianity. Saint Milo is a 6th-century French bishop who is known for his role in the conversion of the Frisians. He is said to have preached the Gospel in Friesland and faced numerous challenges and adversities in his missionary work. Despite this, Milo's steadfast faith and dedication to spreading the word of God led to the conversion of many people. In this way, the name Milo represents not only the theme of mercy and kindness but also the qualities of faith, resilience, and commitment to spreading the teachings of Christ.
